A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the iron bioavailability in the presence of proteins and their digestion products can be predicted by their ability to complex with iron, and that this ability is a function of the chemical structure of the protein.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the iron bioavailability of protein sources is not related to their amino acid content, but to their protein structure.
protein digestion products can enhance iron bioavailability, but the effects depend on the protein source.
iron dialyzability, as measured in vitro, can provide a useful estimate of the bioavailability of dietary iron.
